title: Kamil Pooran Earns Maiden T20I Call-Up for West Indies' India Tour
excerpt: The 30-year-old opener's breakout CPL 2026 season earned him a place in the T20I squad, while Jason Holder is rested and Shimron Hetmyer will join only for the T20Is.
body:
• Cricket West Indies on Saturday announced its squads for the white-ball tour of India, handing opening batter Kamil Pooran a maiden T20I call-up after his breakout CPL 2026 season.
  • The 30-year-old scored 273 runs in eight innings at a strike rate of 159.64 for the St Lucia Kings, with two half-centuries and a best of 81 not out.
  • Veteran all-rounder Jason Holder has been rested from both squads, while Shimron Hetmyer will skip the ODIs and join for the T20I leg. John Campbell returns to the ODI squad from a hamstring injury.
  • West Indies play three ODIs from September 27 to October 3 and five T20Is from October 6 to October 17, departing the Caribbean on September 21.

Pooran's breakthrough

West Indies have handed opening batter Kamil Pooran a maiden T20I call-up for the five-match series in India, rewarding the standout new face of the Caribbean Premier League season. The 30-year-old played eight matches for the St Lucia Kings in CPL 2026 and scored 273 runs at a strike rate of 159.64, with two half-centuries and a best of 81 not out.

A Cricket West Indies release said Pooran's inclusion reflected a "deliberate approach towards identifying and developing emerging talent ahead of the 2028 T20 World Cup," according to ESPNcricinfo. The right-hander averaged 39 across his eight innings, opening consistently for the Kings in a tournament that has long served as West Indies' talent pipeline.

Squad shake-up: Holder rested, Hetmyer partial

The headline omissions tell their own story. Experienced all-rounder Jason Holder, who captained the St Kitts & Nevis Patriots in the CPL, has been "rested" altogether and features in neither squad. Holder has not played an ODI since July 2023 but was part of West Indies' most recent T20I assignment, against Sri Lanka in June.

Shimron Hetmyer, the second-highest run-scorer in CPL 2026 with 367 runs in 12 innings for the Guyana Amazon Warriors at an average of 45.87 and a strike rate of 197.31, was allowed to skip the three-match ODI leg and will link up with the team in India for the five T20Is. The release said he "remains committed" but has been given an "extended recovery period post CPL."

Opener John Campbell returns to the ODI squad after recovering from a hamstring injury that cost him the last two ODIs against New Zealand. Middle-order batter Quentin Sampson, who was part of the West Indies squad at the ICC T20 World Cup earlier this year in India, is among the T20I prospects. Top-order batter Ackeem Auguste has been ruled out of the tour as he recovers from surgery in August, with Jewel Andrew — who last played for West Indies in September 2025 — included in both squads. Shai Hope will captain both sides.

Sammy's long view

"We are looking to build on the momentum from our series win against Sri Lanka, with the long-term goal of developing a strong core of players ahead of the next T20 World Cup. The challenge of playing against the World Champions at home will provide valuable preparation."

— Daren Sammy, West Indies head coach

Sammy said the series also creates a valuable platform to assess players stepping into important roles with a long-term target of competing in the 2027 ODI World Cup. "Playing against the top team in the world presents us with a chance to fine tune and improve our performances as an ODI team which has seen quality performances across the cycle," he said.

The stakes

The series begins with three one-dayers between September 27 and October 3, followed by five T20Is from October 6 to October 17. The squad departs the Caribbean on September 21 and arrives in Thiruvananthapuram on September 23.

The first two ODIs are the final matches of the automatic qualification cycle for the ICC Men's 50-over World Cup — but whatever happens, West Indies cannot overtake their nearest rivals in the qualifying table and will have to take part in the qualifying tournament early next year. The India series, then, is less about qualification arithmetic and more about the rebuild: a young squad, a new opener in Pooran, and a coach openly building toward 2027 and 2028.

For Indian fans, the tour offers a look at the next generation of Caribbean cricket — and for Pooran, a career-defining stage. A call-up on the back of a breakout domestic season is one thing. Proving it against the world champions, in their backyard, is another.

Squads

West Indies ODI squad: Shai Hope (captain), Jewel Andrew, John Campbell, Keacy Carty, Roston Chase, Matthew Forde, Justin Greaves, Amir Jangoo, Alzarri Joseph, Shamar Joseph, Vitel Lawes, Gudakesh Motie, Keemo Paul, Sherfane Rutherford, Jayden Seales.

West Indies T20I squad: Shai Hope (captain), Jewel Andrew, Roston Chase, Matthew Forde, Shimron Hetmyer, Akeal Hosein, Shamar Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Keemo Paul, Kamil Pooran, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Quentin Sampson, Romario Shepherd, Shamar Springer.
nri_angle: Indian cricket fans get a first look at Kamil Pooran and West Indies' next generation during a full white-ball tour of India starting September 27.
